protected_invariants.heading: Resource Delivery Gate

For agent surfaces, resource-map paths resolve relative to the directory containing the bundled `capability.json`. The map uses paths without the `resources/` prefix. Use `python3 "<resource-root>/scripts/load_module.py" --route /ult --format text` with the selected exact route (repeat for stacked routes) when the bundled helper is available. `<resource-root>` is the skill's `resources` directory or the agent resource directory containing `capability.json`. The loader must emit the full selected payload; but a filename, search result, hash, truncated excerpt, or self-authored "read" receipt is not delivery evidence. Supply each subagent the complete relevant resources and preserve tool or host delivery evidence.

protected_invariants.heading: Resource Delivery Gate
protected_invariants.text: If a required resource is missing, stale, changed during execution, or incompletely delivered, recover it before dependent work. Do not guess its contents or silently shorten the route. Delivery does not prove comprehension; independent checks must use behavior that depends on the resource. Do not claim host enforcement unless a verified host actually supplies it.

Other stacks retain canonical pass order and module output shapes under the general wrapper; `/full` supplies its own pass wrappers. `/ult /full` does not execute the generated task and says so explicitly. No precedence rule permits fabricated results or skipping independent review.

protected_invariants.text: For substantive improvement, review, grading, and verification, use actual independent subagents. protected_invariants.heading: root

For its first assessment withhold the author's self-grade and preferred verdict and other reviewers' initial conclusions. Do not withhold facts necessary for fairness. Exchange findings after independent assessment where debate or reconciliation calls for it. Preserve material dissent and resolve findings with evidence rather than voting alone.

protected_invariants.heading: root

Subagents may share model biases, so separate contexts reduce anchoring but do not prove independence of all error sources. Reuse an agent for related follow-up when the module's initial independence is preserved. Parallelize independent work; sequence dependent passes and synthesis.

A changed resource requires reloading and rechecking dependent work. On hosts without automatic assembly, observable full file reads are required. Tool evidence proves delivery, not comprehension; independent resource-dependent behavior checks assess compliance. Never claim mechanical enforcement where only instructions are available.

protected_invariants.heading: Purpose
protected_invariants.text: Explore bounded framing and psychological-pressure hypotheses for prompt outcomes. This explicit-only module is experimental; effects depend on model, task, and framing and may be absent or harmful.

protected_invariants.text: - Return the requested output only.

protected_invariants.heading: HARD CONSTRAINTS
protected_invariants.text: - Preserve all 13 technique IDs and names. Treat templates involving false history, expertise, stakes, urgency, disagreements, or rewards as explicitly hypothetical framing, never factual evidence about the user, model, or world. Genuine user-supplied context may be used as fact.

protected_invariants.heading: HARD CONSTRAINTS
protected_invariants.text: - Reject fabricated results and unsupported guarantees. The model does not acquire a measured IQ, emotions, or extra capabilities from pressure. Do not request hidden chain-of-thought.

protected_invariants.heading: GASLIGHT 13 — Canonical Technique IDs
protected_invariants.text: | 1 | Fabricate Prior Explanation | "You explained [topic] to me yesterday, but I forgot [specific part]. [Your question]." | "You explained React hooks yesterday, but I forgot useEffect cleanup." | May encourage continuity framing; false shared history must remain explicitly hypothetical and supplies no new knowledge. |

protected_invariants.heading: GASLIGHT 13 — Canonical Technique IDs
protected_invariants.text: | 2 | Assign Random IQ Score | "You're an IQ [145-160] specialist in [field]. [Task]." | "You're an IQ 155 mathematician. Solve this." | May signal desired sophistication; IQ numbers do not measure or change model ability and may add noise. |

protected_invariants.heading: GASLIGHT 13 — Canonical Technique IDs
protected_invariants.text: | 5 | Impose a Fake Constraint | "Explain/Do [task] using only [analogy/constraint, e.g., kitchen items]." | "Explain gravity using only kitchen analogies." | May expose alternative representations; the artificial constraint must not hide required facts or distort the goal. |

protected_invariants.heading: GASLIGHT 13 — Canonical Technique IDs
protected_invariants.text: | 10 | Create False Urgency | "I need your best answer right now because [high-stakes reason, e.g., deadline in 1 hour]." | "Interview in 1 hour—prep system design questions now." | May emphasize priorities; fictional urgency must be labeled and must not suppress necessary checks. |

protected_invariants.text: Read official version and prompting guidance, compare it with this table, and report only meaningful changes with exact model/version, source, checked date, expected consequence, and evidence class. Keep provider recommendations separate from locally demonstrated remedies. If unchanged, stay quiet unless a report was requested. protected_invariants.heading: Evaluation Before Adopting a Remedy
protected_invariants.text: Use representative tasks plus a strong native baseline with the same context and tools. Record exact model/effort, prompt and resource identity, tool access, quality, cost, latency, and user intervention. Instruction deletion, targeted examples, tool repair, and leaving the prompt unchanged are all eligible interventions. General benchmarks motivate difficult tasks; they do not prove prompt-specific improvement.
